free_tier.stated: Every workspace starts on Starter at USD 0 with USD 100 in free credits on first adding a payment method; Starter allows 5 concurrent sessions and machines up to 4 cores / 8 GB.
free_tier.notes: The USD 100 is one-time and requires a payment method: Stripe verifies the card with a USD 0 authorization before granting it. The free Starter plan also exists without the credit once the balance runs out.

per_object_cap.stated: The unit is a VM, not an object. The default Small sandbox is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB root disk; the Starter plan caps machines at 4 cores / 8 GB RAM and storage at 100 GiB per workspace.

retention.stated: A sandbox can be paused and resumed with its files and memory kept for later; storage on Starter is 100 GiB per workspace with snapshots, volumes and sticky disks drawing from that pool.

egress.terms: No egress allowance or price per TB is stated on the pricing page; storage is priced at USD 0.20 per GiB per month from the first byte and serving the runner cache is included in the runner rate.

interface_detail: A CLI installed from luxor.ai/install.sh with luxor onboard, plus Go, TypeScript and Python SDKs; sandbox sessions expose command execution, file I/O, preview URLs and SSH.
tooling: luxor CLI (curl -fsSL https://luxor.ai/install.sh | sh), npm @luxorai/sandbox, go.luxor.ai/sandbox and pip luxor-ai SDKs.
chaining: A sandbox can expose a preview URL and mount a workspace volume, so a coding agent can run a service and keep its files between sessions within the same workspace credit pool.

limits.value: USD 100 one-time free credits on adding a payment method; sandbox vCPU USD 0.000014 per second, memory USD 0.0000045 per GiB-second and disk USD 0.00000003 per GiB-second with 5 GiB free
Starter: 5 concurrent sessions, 4 cores / 8 GB machine limit, 100 GiB storage and 5 members per workspace
the USD 100 credit is granted only after adding a card or Link wallet, and each new CLI key needs a device approval click in the browser

limits_note: Billing is per second of active session time; paused sandboxes stop charging and keep files and memory. When the balance runs out, the platform stops starting new sessions until a top-up of at least USD 20 or auto-reload.
binding_note: The USD 100 one-time credit is the first constraint to run out at sustained use; the Starter five-session and 4-core caps are plan limits, and a card is required before the credit even exists.

identity_cost.detail: The free credits page states that after creating an account you add a card or Link wallet from the Billing tab and Stripe verifies it with a USD 0 authorization before the one-time USD 100 credit is granted; the onboarding docs say sign-in or registration is at app.luxor.ai/auth/registration with Google or GitHub, and CLI login requires a browser device approval click. No phone or ID document is stated.

reliability_note: When credits run out, Luxor Agent Cloud stops starting new jobs and sessions until the workspace is topped up by at least USD 20 or auto-reload is enabled; an unpaid invoice interrupts service and cancels running jobs.
confidence_note: Plan limits, per-second rates, the card-gated credit and the sign-in flow are quoted from vendor pricing, free-credits and onboarding pages read on 2026-11-25.

evidence.quote: Every workspace starts on Starter. Numeric limits below are per-workspace maximums, and every plan adds usage-based billing once its included credits are spent.
evidence.proved: the Starter plan is the default and adds usage billing after credits

evidence.quote: New accounts get **$100 in free credits** the first time they add a payment method.
evidence.proved: the USD 100 free credit is one-time and tied to adding a payment method

evidence.quote: Stripe verifies the card with a $0 authorization, and the workspace receives a one-time **$100 credit**.
evidence.proved: a card is verified with a USD 0 authorization to grant the credit

evidence.quote: Billing is metered per second, so users pay only while a session is active.
evidence.proved: sandbox sessions are billed by the second while active

evidence.quote: The hourly figures aggregate those per-second rates: Nano $0.08/hr, Small $0.17/hr (default: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB), Medium $0.33/hr, Large $0.66/hr, XLarge $1.32/hr.
evidence.proved: the sandbox size ladder and the default 2 vCPU / 4 GiB shape

evidence.quote: Sign in or create a Luxor Agent Cloud account (Google or GitHub) at https://app.luxor.ai/auth/registration/.
evidence.proved: registration uses a Google or GitHub account

notes: Luxor Agent Cloud (formerly Tenki) sells disposable Linux VM sandboxes, GitHub Actions runners and a code reviewer from one workspace balance. The default Small sandbox is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB at USD 0.17 per running hour from the per-second rate card, and the free Starter plan allows 5 concurrent sessions with a USD 100 one-time credit that requires adding a card. A paid Team plan raises the limits but does not change the per-second rates. The card requirement to unlock the free credit, and the USD 20 minimum top-up when the balance runs out, are the caveats.
